# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 266
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/266
- **Title**: feat(pack): registry refs + agent packs as parent configs (dm.ai #579)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `feature/pack-registry-and-parent-by-url` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +736
- **Deletions**: -65
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T20:31:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-28T10:45:17Z

## PR Description

## What

Dart port of dm.ai #601 — two agent-pack runtime additions (dm.ai #579): registry refs and packs as parent configs.

### 1. Pack registry refs: `dmtools run <agent>@<version|latest>`

Resolves through the **`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`** env var — the base URL of a flat pack registry (a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.):

- `@latest` looks the version up in `<registry>/catalog.json` (accepts flat `{"agent":"version"}` or nested `{"agents":{...}}`).
- `@1.2.3` → `<registry>/<agent>-<version>.zip`, with the sibling `.sha256` verified by the existing download path.
- The `@` form is **required**, so bare job names, file paths and `.json` files never match; no registry configured → refs fall through to the file flow.

### 2. `parent.path` accepts pack refs

A config's `parent.path` may now be a **local `.zip`, an `http(s)://…​.zip` URL, or a registry ref** — in addition to a filesystem path. The pack parent is unpacked to the verified cache, its own parent chain resolved inside the pack, and its pack-relative paths rewritten to absolute cache paths so they survive the merge with a child living in another pack or repo. `override`/`merge` directives behave as for filesystem parents.

```json
{
  "name": "Teammate",
  "parent": { "path": "pr_review@latest" },
  "params": { "inputJql": "project=MYTEAM" }
}
```

### Tests

- `test/pack/agent_pack_resolver_test.dart` +5: ref detection (hermetic no-registry vs configured), explicit `@version`, `@latest` via catalog (both shapes), unknown-agent error, `.sha256` verification — via a loopback registry server in a separate isolate.
- `test/cli/run_command_processor_test.dart` +3: local pack zip parent merges with parent `jsPath` rewritten into the cache (existing on disk), `#entry.json` override inside a pack parent, non-pack parent still resolves from the filesystem.

Pre-existing env-dependent failures (`doctor_command` / `property_reader_resolution` reading the dev machine's credentials/`dmtools.env`) reproduce identically on `main`.

### Notes

Registry operator publishes `catalog.json` + zips (dmtools-agents' `ci/release_packs.mjs` already does); this PR only consumes the contract. Java counterpart: epam/dm.ai#601.

// formatter wants
final isolate =
    await Isolate.spawn(_registryServerEntry, [readyInbox.sendPort, files]);
```

Part of the same root cause as the `static` job failure — `dart format .` fixes this file and the rest of the PR in one command.

---

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a GitHub-Releases registry base (the PR's first example) will fail on HTTP 302**

The PR description advertises the registry as "a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.". But `SyncHttpClient` never follows redirects:

- isolate bridge: `request.followRedirects = false; // curl parity: `-s` never follows` (`sync_http_bridge.dart:166`)
- curl fallback: `buildArgs()` has no `-L`.

GitHub release assets (`https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>`) answer **302 Found** (redirect to `objects.githubusercontent.com`), so with `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>` every fetch in this feature — `catalog.json` here, the `-<version>.zip`, and the `.sha256` sidecar — gets a 302 and the resolver throws:

```
Failed to read registry catalog: HTTP 302 for <url>
Failed to download pack: HTTP 302 for <url>
```

This is pre-existing behavior for the direct URL-pack path (`_download` is unchanged), but this PR makes the redirecting host the flagship documented use case, so `dmtools run <agent>@latest` fails out of the box against it.

Options:

1. Follow one redirect hop for pack downloads (repo precedent: `github_workflow_logs.dart` and `confluence_client.dart` resolve a single `Location` hop; `SyncHttpResponse.headers` already captures them).
2. Or document the constraint in the PR/library doc — "registry base must serve 200s directly" (Artifactory, raw.githubusercontent with a pinned tag, Pages all qualify) — and say so in the error message when a 3xx comes back.

Either way, worth a regression test with a loopback server that answers 302.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: validate the `@latest` version from `catalog.json` before building the URL**

An explicit `@1.2.3` is charset-constrained by `_registryRef` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]*`, no separators), but the version returned by `_fetchLatestVersion` for `@latest` is interpolated raw into the download URL:

```dart
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

`catalog.json` is untrusted registry content. A version containing `/` or `..` escapes the intended directory on the registry host; `?` injects a query; `#` silently truncates the URL (fragment), producing a confusing 404 that surfaces much later as "Pack has no manifest.json: <name>.zip" or "Entry ... not found in pack".

Note the asymmetry: the **manifest** `agent`/`version` — which only build the local cache path — are validated (`_validateManifestIdentity`), but the **catalog** version — which builds the network request — is not, and it is checked only after the download has been made (and the `.sha256` sidecar skip path only warns).

Suggestion (cheap, fail-fast, closes the traversal vector):

```dart
final safeVersion = RegExp(r'^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$').firstMatch(version);
if (safeVersion == null || version.startsWith('.')) {
  throw AgentPackException('Unsafe version in registry catalog: "$version"');
}
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

and add a test where the catalog advertises a hostile version.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the ref regex captures `<agent>@<version>.zip`, shadowing local pack files**

With a registry configured, a local file literally named `x@1.2.3.zip` no longer resolves as a local pack:

- the version group `[A-Za-z0-9._-]*` matches the token `1.2.3.zip` (dots allowed), so `isRegistryRef('x@1.2.3.zip')` is true;
- `isPack()` checks `isRegistryRef` **before** the local-`.zip`-exists branch, so the file on disk is ignored and the resolver downloads `$registry/x-1.2.3.zip` (agent `x`, version `1.2.3.zip`) instead.

That is a behavior change vs. the no-registry mode, where the existing local file wins (`base.endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()`), and it contradicts the doc comment's promise that "file paths ... never match". Same for `x@latest.zip`.

Unusual filename, so non-urgent, but the fix is one of:

```dart
// option 1: refuse .zip-suffixed versions
RegExp(r'^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)@(latest|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(?<!\.zip))$');
// option 2: local file wins
if (base.toLowerCase().endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()) return true;
if (isRegistryRef(base)) return true;
```

---

### Thread 7 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
💡 **SUGGESTION: malformed `catalog.json` escapes the resolver's error contract**

Every other failure mode in this class throws an `AgentPackException` with a actionable message. Here:

```dart
final catalog = jsonDecode(response.body);
```

- a syntactically invalid `catalog.json` throws a bare `FormatException` — callers/CLI handlers that match on `AgentPackException` (as the tests do) won't catch it;
- a valid-JSON but non-`Map` cat…

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — …

- **Title**: feat(pack): registry refs + agent packs as parent configs (dm.ai #579)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `feature/pack-registry-and-parent-by-url` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +736
- **Deletions**: -65
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T20:31:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-28T10:45:17Z

## PR Description

## What

Dart port of dm.ai #601 — two agent-pack runtime additions (dm.ai #579): registry refs and packs as parent configs.

### 1. Pack registry refs: `dmtools run <agent>@<version|latest>`

Resolves through the **`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`** env var — the base URL of a flat pack registry (a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.):

- `@latest` looks the version up in `<registry>/catalog.json` (accepts flat `{"agent":"version"}` or nested `{"agents":{...}}`).
- `@1.2.3` → `<registry>/<agent>-<version>.zip`, with the sibling `.sha256` verified by the existing download path.
- The `@` form is **required**, so bare job names, file paths and `.json` files never match; no registry configured → refs fall through to the file flow.

### 2. `parent.path` accepts pack refs

A config's `parent.path` may now be a **local `.zip`, an `http(s)://…​.zip` URL, or a registry ref** — in addition to a filesystem path. The pack parent is unpacked to the verified cache, its own parent chain resolved inside the pack, and its pack-relative paths rewritten to absolute cache paths so they survive the merge with a child living in another pack or repo. `override`/`merge` directives behave as for filesystem parents.

```json
{
  "name": "Teammate",
  "parent": { "path": "pr_review@latest" },
  "params": { "inputJql": "project=MYTEAM" }
}
```

### Tests

- `test/pack/agent_pack_resolver_test.dart` +5: ref detection (hermetic no-registry vs configured), explicit `@version`, `@latest` via catalog (both shapes), unknown-agent error, `.sha256` verification — via a loopback registry server in a separate isolate.
- `test/cli/run_command_processor_test.dart` +3: local pack zip parent merges with parent `jsPath` rewritten into the cache (existing on disk), `#entry.json` override inside a pack parent, non-pack parent still resolves from the filesystem.

Pre-existing env-dependent failures (`doctor_command` / `property_reader_resolution` reading the dev machine's credentials/`dmtools.env`) reproduce identically on `main`.

### Notes

Registry operator publishes `catalog.json` + zips (dmtools-agents' `ci/release_packs.mjs` already does); this PR only consumes the contract. Java counterpart: epam/dm.ai#601.

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a GitHub-Releases registry base (the PR's first example) will fail on HTTP 302**

The PR description advertises the registry as "a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.". But `SyncHttpClient` never follows redirects:

- isolate bridge: `request.followRedirects = false; // curl parity: `-s` never follows` (`sync_http_bridge.dart:166`)
- curl fallback: `buildArgs()` has no `-L`.

GitHub release assets (`https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>`) answer **302 Found** (redirect to `objects.githubusercontent.com`), so with `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>` every fetch in this feature — `catalog.json` here, the `-<version>.zip`, and the `.sha256` sidecar — gets a 302 and the resolver throws:

```
Failed to read registry catalog: HTTP 302 for <url>
Failed to download pack: HTTP 302 for <url>
```

This is pre-existing behavior for the direct URL-pack path (`_download` is unchanged), but this PR makes the redirecting host the flagship documented use case, so `dmtools run <agent>@latest` fails out of the box against it.

Options:

1. Follow one redirect hop for pack downloads (repo precedent: `github_workflow_logs.dart` and `confluence_client.dart` resolve a single `Location` hop; `SyncHttpResponse.headers` already captures them).
2. Or document the constraint in the PR/library doc — "registry base must serve 200s directly" (Artifactory, raw.githubusercontent with a pinned tag, Pages all qualify) — and say so in the error message when a 3xx comes back.

Either way, worth a regression test with a loopback server that answers 302.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: validate the `@latest` version from `catalog.json` before building the URL**

An explicit `@1.2.3` is charset-constrained by `_registryRef` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]*`, no separators), but the version returned by `_fetchLatestVersion` for `@latest` is interpolated raw into the download URL:

```dart
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

`catalog.json` is untrusted registry content. A version containing `/` or `..` escapes the intended directory on the registry host; `?` injects a query; `#` silently truncates the URL (fragment), producing a confusing 404 that surfaces much later as "Pack has no manifest.json: <name>.zip" or "Entry ... not found in pack".

Note the asymmetry: the **manifest** `agent`/`version` — which only build the local cache path — are validated (`_validateManifestIdentity`), but the **catalog** version — which builds the network request — is not, and it is checked only after the download has been made (and the `.sha256` sidecar skip path only warns).

Suggestion (cheap, fail-fast, closes the traversal vector):

```dart
final safeVersion = RegExp(r'^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$').firstMatch(version);
if (safeVersion == null || version.startsWith('.')) {
  throw AgentPackException('Unsafe version in registry catalog: "$version"');
}
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

and add a test where the catalog advertises a hostile version.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the ref regex captures `<agent>@<version>.zip`, shadowing local pack files**

With a registry configured, a local file literally named `x@1.2.3.zip` no longer resolves as a local pack:

- the version group `[A-Za-z0-9._-]*` matches the token `1.2.3.zip` (dots allowed), so `isRegistryRef('x@1.2.3.zip')` is true;
- `isPack()` checks `isRegistryRef` **before** the local-`.zip`-exists branch, so the file on disk is ignored and the resolver downloads `$registry/x-1.2.3.zip` (agent `x`, version `1.2.3.zip`) instead.

That is a behavior change vs. the no-registry mode, where the existing local file wins (`base.endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()`), and it contradicts the doc comment's promise that "file paths ... never match". Same for `x@latest.zip`.

Unusual filename, so non-urgent, but the fix is one of:

```dart
// option 1: refuse .zip-suffixed versions
RegExp(r'^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)@(latest|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(?<!\.zip))$');
// option 2: local file wins
if (base.toLowerCase().endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()) return true;
if (isRegistryRef(base)) return true;
```

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;
dmtools also streams the agent's output live into the step log via stderr
mirroring (gh-50). Wiring: `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml`.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 266
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/266
- **Title**: feat(pack): registry refs + agent packs as parent configs (dm.ai #579)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `feature/pack-registry-and-parent-by-url` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +736
- **Deletions**: -65
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T20:31:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-28T10:45:17Z

## PR Description

## What

Dart port of dm.ai #601 — two agent-pack runtime additions (dm.ai #579): registry refs and packs as parent configs.

### 1. Pack registry refs: `dmtools run <agent>@<version|latest>`

Resolves through the **`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`** env var — the base URL of a flat pack registry (a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.):

- `@latest` looks the version up in `<registry>/catalog.json` (accepts flat `{"agent":"version"}` or nested `{"agents":{...}}`).
- `@1.2.3` → `<registry>/<agent>-<version>.zip`, with the sibling `.sha256` verified by the existing download path.
- The `@` form is **required**, so bare job names, file paths and `.json` files never match; no registry configured → refs fall through to the file flow.

### 2. `parent.path` accepts pack refs

A config's `parent.path` may now be a **local `.zip`, an `http(s)://…​.zip` URL, or a registry ref** — in addition to a filesystem path. The pack parent is unpacked to the verified cache, its own parent chain resolved inside the pack, and its pack-relative paths rewritten to absolute cache paths so they survive the merge with a child living in another pack or repo. `override`/`merge` directives behave as for filesystem parents.

```json
{
  "name": "Teammate",
  "parent": { "path": "pr_review@latest" },
  "params": { "inputJql": "project=MYTEAM" }
}
```

### Tests

- `test/pack/agent_pack_resolver_test.dart` +5: ref detection (hermetic no-registry vs configured), explicit `@version`, `@latest` via catalog (both shapes), unknown-agent error, `.sha256` verification — via a loopback registry server in a separate isolate.
- `test/cli/run_command_processor_test.dart` +3: local pack zip parent merges with parent `jsPath` rewritten into the cache (existing on disk), `#entry.json` override inside a pack parent, non-pack parent still resolves from the filesystem.

Pre-existing env-dependent failures (`doctor_command` / `property_reader_resolution` reading the dev machine's credentials/`dmtools.env`) reproduce identically on `main`.

### Notes

Registry operator publishes `catalog.json` + zips (dmtools-agents' `ci/release_packs.mjs` already does); this PR only consumes the contract. Java counterpart: epam/dm.ai#601.

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a GitHub-Releases registry base (the PR's first example) will fail on HTTP 302**

The PR description advertises the registry as "a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.". But `SyncHttpClient` never follows redirects:

- isolate bridge: `request.followRedirects = false; // curl parity: `-s` never follows` (`sync_http_bridge.dart:166`)
- curl fallback: `buildArgs()` has no `-L`.

GitHub release assets (`https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>`) answer **302 Found** (redirect to `objects.githubusercontent.com`), so with `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>` every fetch in this feature — `catalog.json` here, the `-<version>.zip`, and the `.sha256` sidecar — gets a 302 and the resolver throws:

```
Failed to read registry catalog: HTTP 302 for <url>
Failed to download pack: HTTP 302 for <url>
```

This is pre-existing behavior for the direct URL-pack path (`_download` is unchanged), but this PR makes the redirecting host the flagship documented use case, so `dmtools run <agent>@latest` fails out of the box against it.

Options:

1. Follow one redirect hop for pack downloads (repo precedent: `github_workflow_logs.dart` and `confluence_client.dart` resolve a single `Location` hop; `SyncHttpResponse.headers` already captures them).
2. Or document the constraint in the PR/library doc — "registry base must serve 200s directly" (Artifactory, raw.githubusercontent with a pinned tag, Pages all qualify) — and say so in the error message when a 3xx comes back.

Either way, worth a regression test with a loopback server that answers 302.

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: validate the `@latest` version from `catalog.json` before building the URL**

An explicit `@1.2.3` is charset-constrained by `_registryRef` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]*`, no separators), but the version returned by `_fetchLatestVersion` for `@latest` is interpolated raw into the download URL:

```dart
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

`catalog.json` is untrusted registry content. A version containing `/` or `..` escapes the intended directory on the registry host; `?` injects a query; `#` silently truncates the URL (fragment), producing a confusing 404 that surfaces much later as "Pack has no manifest.json: <name>.zip" or "Entry ... not found in pack".

Note the asymmetry: the **manifest** `agent`/`version` — which only build the local cache path — are validated (`_validateManifestIdentity`), but the **catalog** version — which builds the network request — is not, and it is checked only after the download has been made (and the `.sha256` sidecar skip path only warns).

Suggestion (cheap, fail-fast, closes the traversal vector):

```dart
final safeVersion = RegExp(r'^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$').firstMatch(version);
if (safeVersion == null || version.startsWith('.')) {
  throw AgentPackException('Unsafe version in registry catalog: "$version"');
}
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

and add a test where the catalog advertises a hostile version.

💡 **SUGGESTION: the ref regex captures `<agent>@<version>.zip`, shadowing local pack files**

With a registry configured, a local file literally named `x@1.2.3.zip` no longer resolves as a local pack:

- the version group `[A-Za-z0-9._-]*` matches the token `1.2.3.zip` (dots allowed), so `isRegistryRef('x@1.2.3.zip')` is true;
- `isPack()` checks `isRegistryRef` **before** the local-`.zip`-exists branch, so the file on disk is ignored and the resolver downloads `$registry/x-1.2.3.zip` (agent `x`, version `1.2.3.zip`) instead.

That is a behavior change vs. the no-registry mode, where the existing local file wins (`base.endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()`), and it contradicts the doc comment's promise that "file paths ... never match". Same for `x@latest.zip`.

Unusual filename, so non-urgent, but the fix is one of:

```dart
// option 1: refuse .zip-suffixed versions
RegExp(r'^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)@(latest|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(?<!\.zip))$');
// option 2: local file wins
if (base.toLowerCase().endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()) return true;
if (isRegistryRef(base)) return true;
```

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |
| L4 agents suite | external `agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` | dedicated CI job from Phase 4 |

The agents suite (`dmtools run agents/js/unit-tests/run_all.json` under the Dart
runtime, unmodified) is the **primary acceptance gate** — see GOAL.md.

## 7. Style notes

- `dart format` defaults; public API documented (public_docs gate enforces it).
- Keep methods small (complexity ≤ 10, body ≤ 60 lines, params ≤ 6 — the gates
  enforce this; design around it rather than fighting it).
- Generated code (`*.g.dart`, `*.freezed.dart`) is gate-excluded by default —
  don't hand-edit, regenerate.

## 8. fa session reuse (CI machine)

The ai-teammate machine resumes one fa session per ticket instead of starting
cold on every run. Sessions are named deterministically per `repo:GH-<n>:group` —
bug/story/rework share the `dev-write` conversation (a rework continues the
ticket's dev thread), review has its own `dev-review`. The session directory
(`.dmtools/fa-sessions`) travels across CI runs on a dedicated per-issue branch
`fa-sess/gh-<n>`: restored before the run, force-pushed after it, never merged.
For live debugging, `FA_LOG_FILE` (`fa --log-file`) captures the full
untruncated agent transcript, uploaded as the `fa-trace-*` run artifact;

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 266
- **URL**: https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/266
- **Title**: feat(pack): registry refs + agent packs as parent configs (dm.ai #579)
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `feature/pack-registry-and-parent-by-url` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 8
- **Additions**: +736
- **Deletions**: -65
- **Created**: 2026-09-26T20:31:31Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-28T10:45:17Z

## PR Description

## What

Dart port of dm.ai #601 — two agent-pack runtime additions (dm.ai #579): registry refs and packs as parent configs.

### 1. Pack registry refs: `dmtools run <agent>@<version|latest>`

Resolves through the **`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`** env var — the base URL of a flat pack registry (a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.):

- `@latest` looks the version up in `<registry>/catalog.json` (accepts flat `{"agent":"version"}` or nested `{"agents":{...}}`).
- `@1.2.3` → `<registry>/<agent>-<version>.zip`, with the sibling `.sha256` verified by the existing download path.
- The `@` form is **required**, so bare job names, file paths and `.json` files never match; no registry configured → refs fall through to the file flow.

### 2. `parent.path` accepts pack refs

A config's `parent.path` may now be a **local `.zip`, an `http(s)://…​.zip` URL, or a registry ref** — in addition to a filesystem path. The pack parent is unpacked to the verified cache, its own parent chain resolved inside the pack, and its pack-relative paths rewritten to absolute cache paths so they survive the merge with a child living in another pack or repo. `override`/`merge` directives behave as for filesystem parents.

```json
{
  "name": "Teammate",
  "parent": { "path": "pr_review@latest" },
  "params": { "inputJql": "project=MYTEAM" }
}
```

### Tests

- `test/pack/agent_pack_resolver_test.dart` +5: ref detection (hermetic no-registry vs configured), explicit `@version`, `@latest` via catalog (both shapes), unknown-agent error, `.sha256` verification — via a loopback registry server in a separate isolate.
- `test/cli/run_command_processor_test.dart` +3: local pack zip parent merges with parent `jsPath` rewritten into the cache (existing on disk), `#entry.json` override inside a pack parent, non-pack parent still resolves from the filesystem.

Pre-existing env-dependent failures (`doctor_command` / `property_reader_resolution` reading the dev machine's credentials/`dmtools.env`) reproduce identically on `main`.

### Notes

Registry operator publishes `catalog.json` + zips (dmtools-agents' `ci/release_packs.mjs` already does); this PR only consumes the contract. Java counterpart: epam/dm.ai#601.

# pr-266: feat(pack): registry refs + agent packs as parent configs (dm.ai #579)

## Description

## What

Dart port of dm.ai #601 — two agent-pack runtime additions (dm.ai #579): registry refs and packs as parent configs.

### 1. Pack registry refs: `dmtools run <agent>@<version|latest>`

Resolves through the **`DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY`** env var — the base URL of a flat pack registry (a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.):

- `@latest` looks the version up in `<registry>/catalog.json` (accepts flat `{"agent":"version"}` or nested `{"agents":{...}}`).
- `@1.2.3` → `<registry>/<agent>-<version>.zip`, with the sibling `.sha256` verified by the existing download path.
- The `@` form is **required**, so bare job names, file paths and `.json` files never match; no registry configured → refs fall through to the file flow.

### 2. `parent.path` accepts pack refs

A config's `parent.path` may now be a **local `.zip`, an `http(s)://…​.zip` URL, or a registry ref** — in addition to a filesystem path. The pack parent is unpacked to the verified cache, its own parent chain resolved inside the pack, and its pack-relative paths rewritten to absolute cache paths so they survive the merge with a child living in another pack or repo. `override`/`merge` directives behave as for filesystem parents.

```json
{
  "name": "Teammate",
  "parent": { "path": "pr_review@latest" },
  "params": { "inputJql": "project=MYTEAM" }
}
```

### Tests

- `test/pack/agent_pack_resolver_test.dart` +5: ref detection (hermetic no-registry vs configured), explicit `@version`, `@latest` via catalog (both shapes), unknown-agent error, `.sha256` verification — via a loopback registry server in a separate isolate.
- `test/cli/run_command_processor_test.dart` +3: local pack zip parent merges with parent `jsPath` rewritten into the cache (existing on disk), `#entry.json` override inside a pack parent, non-pack parent still resolves from the filesystem.

Pre-existing env-dependent failures (`doctor_command` / `property_reader_resolution` reading the dev machine's credentials/`dmtools.env`) reproduce identically on `main`.

### Notes

Registry operator publishes `catalog.json` + zips (dmtools-agents' `ci/release_packs.mjs` already does); this PR only consumes the contract. Java counterpart: epam/dm.ai#601.

### Thread 4 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a GitHub-Releases registry base (the PR's first example) will fail on HTTP 302**

The PR description advertises the registry as "a GitHub Releases download base, an Artifactory path, etc.". But `SyncHttpClient` never follows redirects:

- isolate bridge: `request.followRedirects = false; // curl parity: `-s` never follows` (`sync_http_bridge.dart:166`)
- curl fallback: `buildArgs()` has no `-L`.

GitHub release assets (`https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>`) answer **302 Found** (redirect to `objects.githubusercontent.com`), so with `DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY=https://github.com/<o>/<r>/releases/download/<tag>` every fetch in this feature — `catalog.json` here, the `-<version>.zip`, and the `.sha256` sidecar — gets a 302 and the resolver throws:

```
Failed to read registry catalog: HTTP 302 for <url>
Failed to download pack: HTTP 302 for <url>
```

This is pre-existing behavior for the direct URL-pack path (`_download` is unchanged), but this PR makes the redirecting host the flagship documented use case, so `dmtools run <agent>@latest` fails out of the box against it.

Options:

1. Follow one redirect hop for pack downloads (repo precedent: `github_workflow_logs.dart` and `confluence_client.dart` resolve a single `Location` hop; `SyncHttpResponse.headers` already captures them).
2. Or document the constraint in the PR/library doc — "registry base must serve 200s directly" (Artifactory, raw.githubusercontent with a pinned tag, Pages all qualify) — and say so in the error message when a 3xx comes back.

Either way, worth a regression test with a loopback server that answers 302.

---

### Thread 5 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: validate the `@latest` version from `catalog.json` before building the URL**

An explicit `@1.2.3` is charset-constrained by `_registryRef` (`[A-Za-z0-9._-]*`, no separators), but the version returned by `_fetchLatestVersion` for `@latest` is interpolated raw into the download URL:

```dart
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

`catalog.json` is untrusted registry content. A version containing `/` or `..` escapes the intended directory on the registry host; `?` injects a query; `#` silently truncates the URL (fragment), producing a confusing 404 that surfaces much later as "Pack has no manifest.json: <name>.zip" or "Entry ... not found in pack".

Note the asymmetry: the **manifest** `agent`/`version` — which only build the local cache path — are validated (`_validateManifestIdentity`), but the **catalog** version — which builds the network request — is not, and it is checked only after the download has been made (and the `.sha256` sidecar skip path only warns).

Suggestion (cheap, fail-fast, closes the traversal vector):

```dart
final safeVersion = RegExp(r'^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$').firstMatch(version);
if (safeVersion == null || version.startsWith('.')) {
  throw AgentPackException('Unsafe version in registry catalog: "$version"');
}
return '$registry/$agent-$version.zip';
```

and add a test where the catalog advertises a hostile version.

---

### Thread 6 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the ref regex captures `<agent>@<version>.zip`, shadowing local pack files**

With a registry configured, a local file literally named `x@1.2.3.zip` no longer resolves as a local pack:

- the version group `[A-Za-z0-9._-]*` matches the token `1.2.3.zip` (dots allowed), so `isRegistryRef('x@1.2.3.zip')` is true;
- `isPack()` checks `isRegistryRef` **before** the local-`.zip`-exists branch, so the file on disk is ignored and the resolver downloads `$registry/x-1.2.3.zip` (agent `x`, version `1.2.3.zip`) instead.

That is a behavior change vs. the no-registry mode, where the existing local file wins (`base.endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()`), and it contradicts the doc comment's promise that "file paths ... never match". Same for `x@latest.zip`.

Unusual filename, so non-urgent, but the fix is one of:

```dart
// option 1: refuse .zip-suffixed versions
RegExp(r'^([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)@(latest|[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*(?<!\.zip))$');
// option 2: local file wins
if (base.toLowerCase().endsWith('.zip') && File(base).existsSync()) return true;
if (isRegistryRef(base)) return true;
```

---

### Thread 7 — `lib/src/pack/agent_pack_resolver.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-09-27):
💡 **SUGGESTION: malformed `catalog.json` escapes the resolver's error contract**

```
